findings.title: align-items mixin passes modern values to legacy box-align properties and emits a nonexistent property
findings.body: The mixin writes `$alignment` unchanged into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those legacy properties use different keywords (`start`/`end` instead of `flex-start`/`flex-end`). `center` and `baseline`, the only values used today, happen to be valid in both. Any future call such as `align-items(flex-start)` will produce invalid legacy declarations, and old browsers will silently ignore them. `-ms-align-items` (line 121) does not exist in any IE/Edge implementation and is dead output. The mixin looks safe for all inputs when it is not.

findings.title: Panel right-alignment now depends on `margin-left: auto`, which legacy flexbox fallbacks don't support
findings.body: The panel used to be pushed right with `float: right`. That was replaced by `margin-left: auto` on a flex item. The new mixins emit legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` fallbacks. In those 2009-era flexbox implementations, auto margins do not absorb free space the way they do in the modern spec. A browser that takes the legacy path will therefore render the user/search panel directly after the title instead of at the right edge. Floats are also ignored on flex items, so there is no fallback. Either drop the legacy-prefix claim or add a legacy-compatible alignment such as `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on the spacer or title.

findings.title: Custom-message paragraph spacing removed
findings.body: `.small-action-desc .custom-message p` changed from `margin: 5px 0` to `margin: 0`. Custom messages are rendered as cooked HTML and can contain several paragraphs. They now run together with no vertical separation. The spacing was not needed to fix the flex centering, so this is an unrelated visual regression.

findings.title: Float declarations inside the new flex container have no effect, so the button no longer right-aligns
findings.body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex`, but `.topic-avatar { float: left }` and `button { float: right }` are left in place. Floats are ignored on flex items. If the button is a flex item of `.small-action`, the intended right alignment is lost and it sits right after the description text. `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1` or auto margin to absorb the free space. The stale float rules are misleading, and the button positioning should be reworked explicitly, for example with `margin-left: auto`.
